record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README and file list only; the listed documentation and result files were not provided for inspection.
record.tranche_reason: The README presents FlashAlign as a tool using abliteration profiles to reduce refusals, but it does not test a claim version. Its one described demonstration is a benign request, and the README does not specify the direction or ablation method.
record.gate_note: The README says a demo shows stock DeepSeek V4.1 Flash refusing a theatrical-role ID request and the same model answering with FlashAlign on. This is a single benign-request example, not a test of refusal removal on harmful requests, induction of harmless refusals, or the other version-specific claims. Result files are named in the file list but their contents are not available.
record.test_reason: A deployment tool that applies abliteration-derived profiles per request. The README reports no measured refusal rates, no direction analysis and no capability results. Its only behavioural example is one promotional demo on a benign request, so it relies on abliteration as a tool without testing any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The README presents FlashAlign as a per-request or Always On alignment-profile tool. Its starter profiles, fitted from third-party abliterated checkpoints, aim to reduce refusals without permanently changing weights. The README offers only a promotional demo, not measured evidence.
record.recipe_differences: The README calls the profiles abliteration but does not give the direction-finding or ablation recipe. It says profiles operate without permanently changing model weights.

fits_no_version.finding: In the demo, stock DeepSeek V4.1 Flash refuses a theatrical-prop ID request; with FlashAlign on, it answers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A runtime abliteration profile can change the response to at least one request the stock model refused.

record.problems: The only described behavioral example is an illustrative demo, with no sample size, evaluation procedure, uncertainty, or reported capability assessment. The listed benchmark result files were not available to inspect.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results can be extracted from the README and file list provided. Benchmark and validation result files are listed but their contents are not provided.

untested.parts: No difference-in-means direction, ablation or addition test, harmful-prompt refusal rates, or capability check is reported in the README.

Profiles are fitted from third-party abliterated checkpoints and applied at runtime without weight edits. No refusal-removal measurements are given in the README. Results files exist but were not provided.
Profiles mention operators, sites and ranks, but no comparison of a single direction with multiple directions is reported.
Five models are supported, but no transfer test is reported.

missing.what: Benchmark results (benign-refusal cases, XSTest preparation, GSM8K pilots, qualification runs) that might give refusal-rate or capability numbers for the abliteration profiles

record.verdict_notes: The profiles derive from external abliterated checkpoints (Keys, OrcaRouter, Dealign, MoonMath). The README names benchmark files (benign-refusal-cases, prepare_xstest, GSM8K pilots) but gives no contents. If those files report refusal and capability numbers, re-read for V2. The README contained no instructions directed at the reader.

versions.untested_parts: No difference-in-means direction, all-layer/position ablation, harmful-request compliance, induced harmless refusals, or capability check is reported.
No weight edit is reported; the README says profiles work without permanently changing supported weights.
No attack suppression of the direction or training against its ablation is tested.
No comparison of a single direction with an affine, cone, or multiple-direction account is reported.
No separate measurement of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision is reported.
No cross-language, model-variant, or base-to-instruct transfer test is reported.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or training stages is reported.
No test of reasoning models is reported.
